build.summary: I built the PCI scenario registry. The four hard-coded PCI_SCENARIOS are now typed PciScenarioDefs (shared Lesion type, several lesions per case, anatomy, patient, setup, start states, hidden axes drawn by seed, variantAxes). They live in a pack file that registry.ts finds by import.meta.glob, with an engine-free sibling core.launch.ts. legacy.ts toPciScenario builds the engine's PciScenario. The legacy target/calcium fields stay in charge of the active lesion, so tests that override `target` and the ladder variants still work. generate.ts resolveScenario(id, variant, {seed}) handles ladder variant ids through the catalogue's pciVariantById/applyPciVariant; any other variant string is treated as a seed. geometry.ts PciGeom gained lesions[] and targetIdx, plus lesionGeom() and setTarget(g, idx), which returns a new geometry and leaves the input unchanged. actions/scenario.ts: scenarioCase now builds every lesion, dominance, root, variants, grafts, scenarioId and case events; PCI_SCENARIOS and SCENARIO_BY_ID are taken from the registry; new startPci() opens a named start ('guide-in-root' default, 'guide-engaged', 'wire-across', which parks the wire in the true lumen beyond the lesion). catalogue.ts now builds PCI_BASES from registry defs marked ladderBase; the calcium rule comes from def.variantAxes, and every ladder variant is unchanged. src/ui/pci/launch.ts resolves launch params or a full-case transfer (transfer first) into scenario, start, mode, technique/step/workspace and events, through takePciLaunch() and the usePciLaunch() hook. The core four give the same initPci state, the same anatomy case fields and the same coronary-tree radii as before, so the renderer output should not change.

Snapshots of the three listed files that already existed (actions/scenario.ts, geometry.ts, catalogue.ts) are in datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/pci-scenario-registry/, with .started. The other listed files are new.

Changes and design choices:
- The core packs keep their content word for word. The lesions add only fields the old data already implied: calcium grades, role 'target', morphology 'thrombus' for lcx-stemi and 'cto' for rca-cto, sites ['cto'] for rca-cto, and a case event 'stemi' for lcx-stemi. No eGFR, CTO cap shape, thrombus grade or guide alternatives were invented; those fields are left absent.
- Lesson links in core.launch.ts are the lessons whose PCI-lab drill task names the scenario (for example 'In the PCI lab (calcified mid-RCA)'). rca-cto also links cases cx-case-rca-cto and cp-cto-antegrade-case-rca. I found them with a scratch vite-node script over TRACKS.
- core.launch.ts declares the 25 practice ladder variants (pci-<id>~L0..L24); a test checks the count against LADDER_PARAMS. Exam variants are left undeclared, so lessons cannot link them.
- setup.guideInRoot defaults to true, as the design says, so the default start is 'guide-in-root' (guide not engaged). The current AngioPci.tsx still calls initialPci(s), which opens with the guide engaged. Nothing changes until the lab shell adopts startPci; its owner should confirm the default start.
- setup.french 7 is applied by startPci through initialGuide; initialPci in state.ts (not mine) still hard-codes 6.
- PCI_BASES order changed from lad-focal, lcx-stemi, rca-calcified, rca-cto to registry order (lad-focal, rca-calcified, lcx-stemi, rca-cto). Nothing depends on the order; logbook uses find().
- ladderFor still reports playableRungs 1 for PCI, because the lab UI does not take variants yet.
- PCI_SCENARIOS leaves out held-out definitions and keeps lad-focal first, since the core pack is always ordered first.
- New facade exports (startPci, startInitOptions, MP_START_WIRE) come through `export *`, which facade.test.ts allows.
- No renderer file was touched, and the core four's tree radii are identical, so no realism re-capture is needed.

review.verdict: Approve with minor fixes. The design is fully and correctly implemented within the package's files. Of the 12 listed files, three existed before (geometry.ts, actions/scenario.ts, catalogue.ts) and their diffs against the snapshots match the builder's report. The others are new, plus the extra test src/simulation/pci/scenarios/tips.test.ts, which the rules allow. The other files under src/ changed after .started are src/simulation/session/{autopilot,caseSession,scenarios/index,scenarios.test,ledgerTips.test}.ts, src/state/useProcedureStore{,.test}.ts, src/ui/lab/useLabTips.ts, src/ui/sections/ProcedureLab.tsx and src/ui/sim/Simulator.tsx. Each is listed by another package (proc-foundation-scenarios-ledger, diag-tip-context, found-lab-session-plumbing and others), and none imports the PCI registry. I ran the checks myself. The 3 package test files passed 24/24. facade.test.ts, angioPci.test.ts and progress.test.ts passed 88/88. practiceIndex.test.ts and reachability.test.ts passed. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` is clean. Three things from the report hold up. First, the core four still build the same state: the frozen pre-registry literal gives a deep-equal initPci state, the same anatomy-case fields and the same tree radii. Second, the renderer is unaffected: coronaryTree.ts derives calcium and thrombus from lesion.kind only, so the new lesion fields (calcium, morphology, sites, role) on AnatomyCase.lesions do not change it. Third, the lesson links are justified: I checked all 86 core.launch.ts lessonIds against their drill task text, and each names its scenario, with one exception (finding 4). Every ladder variant (L and X) matches the old algorithm, and the engine defaults are unchanged (initialPci in state.ts is untouched). The current AngioPci.tsx still calls initialPci(s), so behaviour in the live lab is unchanged. No new clinical numbers are unsourced: MP_START_WIRE is labelled MODEL PARAMETER in code. No ground truth reaches a live screen (the hidden draws are only returned in ResolvedPciScenario), and there are no per-frame allocations. Two failures elsewhere are real and not this package's. content.test.ts fails 6 'lab launch links' fixture tests; core.launch.ts adds about 88 lesson-id errors to failures that default.launch.ts already caused, and the fix belongs to the found-launch-links owner. The mentor.test.ts failure on the diagnostic 'over-rotation' card is unrelated. The browser criterion, and making the tips reachable in the lab, depend on pci-lab-shell-session (AngioPci.tsx) and pci-tip-context, as the builder reported.

findings.problem: The hook does not keep the 'transfer first' rule that takePciLaunch() and the file header promise. On mount, useLabHandover delivers a pending transfer first, then useLabLaunch delivers a pending link. onLaunch is therefore called twice, and the link's scenario, applied last, replaces the full-case transfer and its patient. No test covers usePciLaunch.
findings.fix: In the link callback, drop or defer a link when a transfer was delivered in the same mount, or when peekHandover(PCI_SIM) is not null. For example, keep a ref `tookHandover` that the handover callback sets, and have the link callback return early when it is set during the initial mount pass (or re-queue the link). Alternatively, run one effect that calls takePciLaunch() on mount and then subscribes to both stores. Add a test with both stores pending before mount that asserts onLaunch receives only the transfer.

findings.problem: The checks that each start opens at its declared phase (pciTipContext(startPci(...)).phase === start.phase), that the 'across' start leaves the wire out of the danger zone, and that the default start resolves all loop over CORE only. start.phase is only logged by startPci and never enforced. A future pack whose start declares, say, phase 'lesion-prep' with wire 'in-guide' would pass every registry check while opening in a different phase.
findings.fix: Loop over PCI_SCENARIO_DEFS instead of CORE. For every def and every start, build the geometry, call startPci and expect pciTipContext(st, g.lesion).phase toBe start.phase. Expect guide.engaged toBe start.guideEngaged, and for wire 'across' expect tipMm > g.lesion.endMm and wire.distal.inDanger false. Also assert that GUIDE_BY_ID[def.setup.guideDefault] exists for every def (in the test, so the registry stays engine-free).

fix.notes:
I applied 5 findings, rejected 1 and passed 2 to outOfScope.

1. usePciLaunch now keeps the transfer-first rule (src/ui/pci/launch.ts). Before, the hook called two store hooks, so a link pending beside a transfer could reach onLaunch after it and replace the transfer and its patient. Now takePciLaunch() empties both stores. When a transfer is present it wins, and any pending link is set aside and named in problems ('a pending link to "<id>" was set aside: the transfer is taken first'). The new exported subscribePciLaunch(onLaunch) runs takePciLaunch() once at mount, then subscribes to both stores for later arrivals through subscribeLabHandover and subscribeLabLaunch. usePciLaunch wraps it in a single useEffect. In launch.test.ts, the transfer-before-link test now expects the link to be set aside instead of returned by a second take. A new test puts both a link and a transfer in place before mount and checks that onLaunch receives only the transfer, then each later link and transfer, and nothing after unsubscribe. Nothing else in src imports this module.

2. Start states are now checked for every registered scenario, not only the core four (scenarios.test.ts). The new test loops over PCI_SCENARIO_DEFS and every start. It checks the tip phase against start.phase, guide.engaged against start.guideEngaged, and the wire: for 'across', the tip is beyond lesion.endMm and distal.inDanger is false; otherwise tipMm < 0. It also checks that the default start is logged, and that GUIDE_BY_ID has setup.guideDefault and every guidesAcceptable entry. The check lives in the test, so the registry stays engine-free.

3. guidesAcceptable and guideInRoot are now used. PciScenarioExtras gained guidesAcceptable; legacy.ts toPciScenario copies setup.guidesAcceptable into it, and scenarioCase now sets acceptableCatheters to the scenario's guide followed by those guides, without duplicates. The core four set none, so their case is unchanged; a test confirms this and also covers a fixture that sets them. For guideInRoot, defProblems() now reports a definition whose default start contradicts an explicitly set setup.guideInRoot. The types.ts doc now says the default start decides where the lab opens.

4. Two fixes to the ladder bases. First, collectPciScenarios now reports a second non-held-out ladderBase for the same EPA as '<where>: second ladderBase for EPA <epa> (first <id>)'. A test covers it, and the PCI_BASES doc in catalogue.ts says there is one base per EPA. Second, the calcium axis is renamed: PciVariantAxes.calcium is now calciumGrades, documented as the two grades a variant takes (the first 60% of the time, MODEL PARAMETER; a pair, not a range). PciBase.calciumRange in catalogue.ts is now calciumGrades, and core.ts is updated. The draw is unchanged, so every ladder variant id and its values stay the same; the existing ladder test still passes. Nothing outside these files used the old names.

5. The registry header comment now lists the new problem kinds.
